Repo: c:\Users\Micro\3D Objects\DEV\deliveryhub_white_label (frontend, React/Vite) with git submodule server_delivery (NestJS backend). Supabase Postgres.

I'm planning a big new "módulo RESTAURANTE" feature (dine-in: mesas/comandas/garçons/caixa/KDS por setor/PDV). Before designing it I need full understanding of the EXISTING cash-register ("caixa") module, since it already handles opening/closing a cash register and reconciling delivery orders — I want to extend/reuse it rather than duplicate.

Please read and report on:
1. `supabase/migrations/20260609000002_caixas_table.sql`, `20260610000001_saldo_caixa.sql`, `20260610000006_caixas_entradas.sql` — full schema of `caixas` table and any related tables/columns (including `orders.caixa_id`). Note all columns, types, constraints, RLS policies.
2. `src/pages/restaurante-financeiro/index.jsx`, `CaixaAtualPanel.jsx`, `HistoricoCaixasPanel.jsx` — how the frontend currently opens/closes a caixa, what data it displays, what actions are available (sangria/saída, fechamento, resumo).
3. `src/pages/restaurante-dashboard/FecharCaixaModal.jsx` — how closing a caixa is triggered from the dashboard, what it sends to the backend.
4. Backend: search `server_delivery/src/restaurante/restaurante.service.ts` and `restaurante.controller.ts` for any caixa-related endpoints/methods (abrir, fechar, resumo, saida). Also check `server_delivery/src/pedidos/pedidos.service.ts` for how `caixa_id` gets attached to an order.
5. `src/services/restauranteService.js` — list the caixa-related API call functions (names + endpoints they hit).
6. Confirm whether there's any existing concept of "operador de caixa" login/identity, or if caixa is just tied to the restaurant owner's own login (no separate operator auth).

Report back: full caixa data model, full list of existing caixa-related files (frontend + backend + migrations) with their responsibilities, and whether/how a NEW dine-in comanda/mesa flow could plug into `orders.caixa_id` (i.e., can a comanda become an `orders` row when closed, so it flows through the exact same caixa reconciliation that delivery orders already use?). Be concrete and cite file:line for key facts. Under 600 words.

-- Tabela de caixas operacionais por restaurante
CREATE TABLE public.caixas (
  id            SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  restaurant_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES public.restaurants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  nome_operador TEXT NOT NULL,
  valor_inicial DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'aberto'
                CHECK (status IN ('aberto', 'fechado', 'expirado')),
  aberto_em     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  fechado_em    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  saidas        JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  resumo        JSONB,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_caixas_restaurant_status ON public.caixas (restaurant_id, status);

-- FK em orders para rastrear a qual caixa cada pedido pertence
ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD COLUMN caixa_id INT REFERENCES public.caixas(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;

-- RLS: apenas owner do restaurante acessa seus caixas
ALTER TABLE public.caixas ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY "restaurant_owner_own_caixas" ON public.caixas
  FOR ALL
  USING (
    restaurant_id IN (
      SELECT id FROM public.restaurants WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- Service role bypassa RLS (backend usa service_role)
CREATE POLICY "service_role_all_caixas" ON public.caixas
  FOR ALL
  TO service_role
  USING (true)
  WITH CHECK (true);

content.text:
This confirms only owner-level auth (Supabase JWT user → restaurant owner). `nome_operador` is just a free-text field typed in at open time, not a real login/identity. Now I have everything needed.

## Report: Existing Caixa Module

**Data model** (`supabase/migrations/20260609000002_caixas_table.sql:2-19`, `20260610000001_saldo_caixa.sql`, `20260610000006_caixas_entradas.sql`):

- `public.caixas`: `id SERIAL PK`, `restaurant_id INT FK→restaurants`, `nome_operador TEXT` (free text, not an auth identity), `valor_inicial DECIMAL(12,2)`, `status TEXT CHECK IN ('aberto','fechado','expirado')`, `aberto_em`/`fechado_em TIMESTAMPTZ`, `saidas JSONB[]` (sangrias), `entradas JSONB[]` (added later), `resumo JSONB` (computed totals snapshot at close), `destinacao_fechamento JSONB` (conference/reconciliation result: `dinheiro_contado`, `diferenca`, `conferencia_aprovada`), `created_at`. Index on `(restaurant_id, status)`.
- `orders.caixa_id INT FK→caixas ON DELETE SET NULL` — this is the link point: every order is tagged with whichever caixa was `status='aberto'` at creation time.
- `restaurants.saldo_caixa DECIMAL(12,2)` — persistent physical balance carried across sessions.
- RLS: owner-only via `restaurant_id IN (SELECT id FROM restaurants WHERE user_id = auth.uid())`; separate `service_role` bypass policy for the backend.

**Backend** (`server_delivery/src/restaurante/restaurante.controller.ts:187-227` + `.service.ts:704-966`):
Endpoints under `/restaurante/caixa*`, all behind `RestaurantOwnerGuard`: `GET caixa` (current), `POST caixa/abrir`, `POST caixa/fechar`, `POST caixa/:id/conferencia` (manager approval), `POST caixa/fechar-e-transferir` (close + open new in one step, for shift handoff), `GET caixa/historico`, `GET caixa/:id` (detail incl. linked orders), `POST caixa/saida`, `POST caixa/entrada`. In `pedidos.service.ts:188-208`, order creation queries the currently open caixa and stamps `caixa_id` on the new `orders` row — this is the exact mechanism a dine-in flow would reuse.

**Frontend**: `src/services/restauranteService.js:110-130` wraps all the above endpoints (`getCaixa`, `abrirCaixa`, `fecharCaixa`, `fecharETransferir`, `adicionarSaida`, `adicionarEntrada`, `getCaixaHistorico`, `getCaixaDetalhe`, `aprovarConferencia`). `src/pages/restaurante-financeiro/index.jsx` is the main financial page: shows `CaixaAtualPanel` when open, pending-conference approvals, period reports (day/month/year/range) with totals by payment method, and `HistoricoCaixasPanel` (past sessions, expandable detail with linked orders/movements). `CaixaAtualPanel.jsx` renders live KPIs (espécie esperada, digital total, entradas/saídas) and triggers sangria/adição modals plus `FecharCaixaModal`. `FecharCaixaModal.jsx` (`src/pages/restaurante-dashboard/FecharCaixaModal.jsx`) has two views: blocks closing if there are open orders (offering "transferir" to a new operator/caixa instead), otherwise shows a reconciliation screen (`dinheiro_contado` input → computes `diferenca` vs `especie_calculada`) and posts to `fecharCaixa`/`fecharETransferir`.

**Operator identity**: confirmed there is **no separate operator login**. Auth is entirely via `RestaurantOwnerGuard` (`server_delivery/src/auth/restaurant-owner.guard.ts:12-30`), which resolves `req.restaurantId` from the Supabase JWT `userId` → `restaurants.user_id`. `nome_operador` on `caixas` is just a free-text label typed when opening — no distinct garçom/operator credentials exist anywhere.

**Plugging in a dine-in flow**: Since `orders.caixa_id` is populated generically at order-creation time by looking up the restaurant's open caixa, a new comanda/mesa module can reuse this untouched — when a comanda is closed, insert (or finalize) an `orders` row (or reuse existing order-creation code path) so it gets `caixa_id` stamped the same way, flowing straight into the existing `resumo`/`saidas`/`entradas`/reconciliation and all of `restaurante-financeiro`. Main gap to address before building mesas/garçons: no per-operator auth exists, so a real "operador de caixa" (garçom) login system would need to be added if the new module requires per-waiter accountability beyond the free-text `nome_operador` field.
